entities.summary:
Servius Cornelius Maluginensis Cossus was a Roman senator who played a pivotal role in shaping the early Roman Republic.

Born into a prominent patrician family, Servius Cornelius rose to prominence through his intelligence, strategic thinking, and connections within Rome's elite circles. His election as consul in 485 BC reflects his status as one of the most influential figures of his time.

Maluginensis Cossus was known for his leadership during the tumultuous period following the expulsion of the king Lucius Tarquinius Superbus in 509 BC, a date that marked the beginning of the Roman Republic. His actions contributed to the establishment of the Senate and helped secure Rome's early victories against its neighboring states.

Despite his significance, there is limited information available about Servius Cornelius Maluginensis Cossus beyond his electoral records and historical accounts from ancient sources.

Servius Cornelius Maluginensis was a Roman senator who was elected consul in 485 BC.
